p01.why: The hidden rvalue reference extends the temporary array, each name is an lvalue so decltype((a)) is int&, and a can be assigned 5.

p02.why: Neither class has a member function template named get, so argument-dependent lookup finds lib::get, giving 1, 2, 3, 4.

p03.why: The calls to get occur in element order, so order holds 0 then 1.

p04.why: The list of names must not be in parentheses.

p05.why: The address of a binding to a bit-field must not be taken.

p06.why: decltype(auto) is not allowed in a structured binding.

p07.why: A braced array initializer is valid; Clang 22, GCC, and EDG accept it, while Clang 18.1.3 rejects it (Q-0015).

p08.why: x is already declared in the same scope by the structured binding.

p09.why: A parenthesized initializer is allowed, and the array is copied.

p10.why: The member get template gives the elements, and each name has the tuple_element type, int and double.

p11.why: The array has three elements and there are two names.

p12.why: An empty list of names is not allowed; Clang reports it as a pedantic diagnostic, which -pedantic-errors makes an error.

p13.why: A structured binding must not be constexpr; Clang and GCC accept it only as an extension and reject it under -pedantic-errors.

p14.why: For a member of reference type, decltype of the name is that reference type, int&.

p15.why: Member lookup finds a member function template get, so e.get<i>() is used, giving 100 + 101 = 201.

p16.why: The hidden variable must not be a union.

p17.why: The declaration must not have other declarators.

p18.why: Argument-dependent lookup finds lib::get, giving 1 and 2.

p19.why: The array is copied into the hidden variable and the names refer to its elements.

p20.why: tuple_size<S> is complete but has no value member, so the names refer to the data members (Q-0048).

p22.why: decltype gives each member's declared type with the hidden variable's qualifiers added, so p is int, q const double, r int, u const int.

p23.why: get is in the global namespace, and only argument-dependent lookup in lib is used, so the get call is not valid.

p24.why: An explicit type is not allowed.

p25.why: std::tuple_element<0, P> is only declared, so its type member does not exist.

p26.why: A name must not occur in the initializer of its own declaration.

p27.why: With &, the names refer to the elements of a itself.

p28.why: Each get result initializes a hidden reference that keeps the Token alive while the names exist, so alive is 2, the sum is 3, and both end at the block.

p29.why: A structured binding must not be a class member.

p30.why: x refers to a mutable member, so it can be changed even though the hidden variable is const.

p31.why: The private members are accessible in a friend function.

p32.why: All members are in the base class B, which is allowed.

p33.why: constinit is not valid; Clang and GCC 16 reject it, while EDG 7.0 and GCC 14 accept it (Q-0107).

p34.why: The hidden const reference extends the temporary Two until the names end, so '|' is logged first.

p35.why: The binding refers to the bit-field, so assigning 2 changes f.bits.

p36.why: Without a reference the array is copied, so changing x does not change a.

p37.why: The hidden variable must not have scalar type.

p38.why: Member a is private and not accessible at the declaration.

p39.why: inline is not a valid specifier for a structured binding.

p40.why: A structured binding declaration must have an initializer.

p41.why: A structured binding must not be a template.

p42.why: A constrained auto is not allowed; Clang and GCC reject it, EDG 7.0 accepts it (Q-0016).

p43.why: A structured binding must not be a function parameter.

p44.why: The members are split between D and its base B.

p45.why: The names refer to the copied members, 1, 2.5, and 3.

p46.why: S has two members and there is one name.

p48.why: The members include an anonymous union.

p49.why: The array is copied, so a later change to arr does not reach a.

p50.why: static and thread_local are allowed, at namespace and block scope.

p51.why: The names in one declaration must be different.

p52.why: The tuple size is 2 and there are three names.

p53.why: extern is not a valid specifier for a structured binding.

p54.why: Two _ names are not allowed in C++23; Clang and GCC accept them only as an extension and reject them under -pedantic-errors.

p55.why: With & get receives an lvalue and returns 1; with && and plain auto it receives an xvalue and returns 2, so the sum is 122.
